叫.meaning: A choir teacher taps a <part>tuning fork</part> on the piano, and instead of a soft hum, a tiny <part>mouth</part> on its handle bellows 'TUESDAY!' Everyone jumps out of their seats. That fork can't hum at all; it can only <kanji>shout</kanji>.
叫.on: Next it yells '<sound>Kyo</sound>to!', holding the first part until the windows rattle.
叫.kun: A lady in a <sound>sa</sound>ri drops her <sound>ke</sound>ttle in fright.

釈.meaning: A bear teacher lays her <part>paw</part> on the chalkboard beside a tape <part>measure</part> to show how big a fish she caught, then talks for an hour about why it was really twice that size. The cubs nod, lost. Her lesson is one long <kanji>explanation</kanji>.
釈.on: The fish, she insists, was nearly the size of a <sound>shar</sound>k.
釈.kun: She ends by drawing it on <sound>to</sound>p of a stove, with a <sound>coo</sound>k frying it.

盲.meaning: A stonemason carves a grand <part>tombstone</part> for an old pirate and adds one carved <part>eye</part> with a patch over it, as the pirate wished. Crows land on it and peer into the stone eye, puzzled: it sees nothing. It is <kanji>blind</kanji>.
盲.on: Every Sunday the groundskeeper's <sound>mo</sound>wer hums slowly around it.

凍.meaning: A man walks <part>east</part> to watch the sunrise and stands there admiring it so long that <part>ice</part> creeps up his boots, his beard and his nose. By noon he's a smiling statue with pigeons on his hat. He's completely <kanji>frozen</kanji>.
凍.on: Only his big <sound>toe</sound> still wiggles inside his boot.
凍.kun: A kid sticks an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne in his hand, and it never melts.

距.meaning: A <part>giant</part> cowboy wants his horse to go faster, so he straps a whole windmill wheel to the heel of each <part>foot</part>. It spins and jingles as he walks, ploughing deep grooves across the prairie. That's one big <kanji>spur</kanji>.
距.on: He stops at a <sound>kio</sound>sk for coffee, and the jingling wakes the whole street.
距.kun: A <sound>he</sound>n and a <sound>du</sound>ck keep well back from his spinning heels.

蓄.meaning: A sheep who doesn't trust winter hides mouthfuls of <part>grass</part> under the barn floor every day while the other <part>livestock</part> nap. By December she's perched on a hay mountain up to the rafters. She has managed to <kanji>amass</kanji> a fortune in snacks.
蓄.on: She tops the pile with one <sound>chic</sound>kpea, like a cherry on a cake.
蓄.kun: She hides a <sound>ta</sound>co, a <sound>coo</sound>kie and a tube of <sound>wa</sound>sabi in there too.
